```{r}
#| label: setup
#| context: setup
library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
library(lubridate)

# Make the logo available to the live Shiny server.
addResourcePath("www", normalizePath("www"))

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

# Use this message when the selected filters leave no records.
empty_plot <- function() {
  plotly_empty() %>%
    layout(title = list(text = "No records match these inputs.", y = .5),
           xaxis = list(visible = FALSE), yaxis = list(visible = FALSE))
}

# Calculate daily changes before removing the December 31 baseline.
df <- read_csv("new_england_covid.csv") %>%
  mutate(date = mdy(date)) %>%
  arrange(state, date) %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  mutate(new_cases = cases - lag(cases), new_deaths = deaths - lag(deaths)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(date >= as.Date("2021-01-01"))
```

# Plots

## {.sidebar}

Use four input types together: a dropdown, state checkboxes, a date
range, and radio buttons. Empty selections display an explanatory message.
New reports may include negative corrections.

```{r}
#| label: sidebar-inputs
selectInput("metric", "Measure", choices = c("Cases" = "cases", "Deaths" = "deaths"))
checkboxGroupInput("states", "States to include", choices = sort(unique(df$state)),
                   selected = c("Connecticut", "Massachusetts", "Rhode Island"))
dateRangeInput("dates", "Reporting date range",
               start = min(df$date), end = max(df$date),
               min = min(df$date), max = max(df$date))
radioButtons("display", "Display totals as",
             choices = c("Cumulative" = "cumulative", "Newly reported" = "new"),
             selected = "cumulative")

textOutput("selection_note")
```

## Row

```{r}
#| label: plot-one-output

plotlyOutput("p1")
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-two-output
```

# Data Notes

::: {.card title="Data and interpretation"}

The bundled file is a New England subset of `us-states.csv` from the
earlier coursework. It contains six states and the 2021 reporting period,
plus December 31, 2020 as a baseline for calculating changes on January 1.
That baseline is excluded from the displayed records.

Cases and deaths are cumulative reported totals, not population rates.
Newly reported values are differences between consecutive cumulative
totals. They can be negative when historical reports are corrected;
those corrections are retained. Comparing raw totals does not establish
that one state had a higher individual risk.

The date control uses real reporting dates, parsed with `mdy()`. The table
shows the same state-day records selected for the plots. Include
`new_england_covid.csv` and `logo.png` when publishing the QMD.

:::

```{r}
#| label: server
#| context: server
filtered <- reactive({
  req(input$dates)
  df %>% filter(state %in% input$states,
                date >= input$dates[1], date <= input$dates[2])
})

output$selection_note <- renderText({
  paste(format(nrow(filtered()), big.mark = ","), "state-day records selected")
})

measure_column <- reactive({
  req(input$metric, input$display)
  if (input$display == "cumulative") input$metric else paste0("new_", input$metric)
})

measure_label <- reactive({
  paste(if (input$display == "cumulative") "Cumulative reported" else "Newly reported",
        input$metric)
})

# Plot 1: Follow the selected measure over time.
output$p1 <- renderPlotly({
  d <- filtered()
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(empty_plot())
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = date, y = .data[[measure_column()]], color = state)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .8) + geom_point(size = .7) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
    labs(x = "Reporting date", y = measure_label(), color = "State")
  ggplotly(p)
})

# Plot 2: Compare either the last cumulative total or net new reports in the interval.
output$p2 <- renderPlotly({
  d <- filtered()
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(empty_plot())
  if (input$display == "cumulative") {
    totals <- d %>% group_by(state) %>%
      slice_max(date, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>%
      transmute(state, value = .data[[input$metric]])
    axis_label <- paste("Cumulative", input$metric, "at last selected date")
  } else {
    totals <- d %>% group_by(state) %>%
      summarise(value = sum(.data[[measure_column()]]), .groups = "drop")
    axis_label <- paste("Net newly reported", input$metric, "in selected period")
  }
  p <- ggplot(totals, aes(x = reorder(state, value), y = value)) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + coord_flip() +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
    labs(x = "State", y = axis_label)
  ggplotly(p)
})

output$tbl <- renderDT({
  filtered() %>% select(date, state, cases, deaths, new_cases, new_deaths) %>%
    mutate(date = format(date, "%Y-%m-%d")) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10, paging = TRUE, searching = TRUE,
                   dom = "lftip", scrollX = TRUE,
                   language = list(info = "Showing _START_ to _END_ of _TOTAL_ records",
                                   infoFiltered = "(filtered from _MAX_ total records)")))
}, server = TRUE)
```
